verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verse.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verse.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verse.why: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

prasang.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
prasang.story_hook: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
prasang.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

verse.for_you: That 2am replay is worry eating the fuel you give it. You do not have to keep feeding it. The conversation is over.
verse.try_today: Notice the fuel you are adding to the fire of worry right now.
verse.scene_line: You sit awake while the fire of 2019 burns from your own attention.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
worry is shown to live on the attention it is fed

verse.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verse.setting: Uddalaka explains sleep to his son.
verse.sanskrit: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा बन्धनमेवोपश्रयत एवमेव खलु सोम्य तन्मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेवोपश्रयते प्राणबन्धनꣳ हि सोम्य मन इति ॥
verse.line: Like a bird on a string, the mind flies everywhere, finds no rest, and returns to the breath.
verse.translation: As a bird tied by a string flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down at the very place it is tied, so, dear one, the mind flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down on the breath; for the mind is tied to the breath.
verse.why: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasang.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasang.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasang.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

verse.try_today: Notice where your mind settles when it finds no other resting place today.

why: the flying about ends in rest, every night
the restless mind is not broken; it has a home it returns to

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha describes King Janaka after his awakening, still ruling his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
verse.translation: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.try_today: Let the replay end. Smile at the room around you.
verse.scene_line: You are the king who hears the sages but stays to rule the day.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
a picture of a mind not living ahead or behind

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6: the first practice for a racing mind.
verse.line: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
verse.translation: The first lesson, then, is to sit for some time and let the mind run on. The mind is bubbling up all the time. It is like that monkey jumping about. Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch. … But you will find that each day the mind's vagaries are becoming less and less violent, that each day it is becoming calmer.
verse.why: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

prasang.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
prasang.summary: The mind is a monkey made drunk by desire, stung by jealousy and possessed by pride. The first practice is to sit and watch it without fighting; each day it grows calmer. Then take up one idea and let it fill your life.
prasang.story_hook: There was a monkey, restless as all monkeys are; someone gave it wine, then a scorpion stung it, and then a demon got into it.
prasang.lesson: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

verse.try_today: Notice the mind jumping without fighting it.
verse.scene_line: You sit still as the mind of a student jumps about in New York.

why: calm arrives by itself, day by day
a sitting practice to repeat

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: You replay that 2019 conversation at 2am, trying to fix what is already fixed. The mind wanders because it thinks it can change what happened. It cannot.
verse.try_today: Let the thoughts come. Do not follow them.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet of 2am, while the mind replays a conversation that is already over.

why: Vishramyatam

story.title: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
story.story_hook: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
story.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
story.teaser: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.for_you: You are trying to force the mind still, but the swinging only grows louder. Let the thoughts run. Then turn back and ask what is doing the replaying.

verse.line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.
verse.translation: It sets foot even where no one can go; even when satisfied it strives in vain; it never stays long in one place: craving is a restless monkey.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.

verse.for_you: You are caught in a loop from 2019, replaying words at 2am. The mind reaches where it cannot go, and craving is a restless monkey that never stays long in one place.
verse.try_today: Notice where the mind reaches today, and let it be there without feeding it.

why: never long in one place
My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.for_you: You keep replaying that 2019 conversation at 2am, caught in a river of hope where every wave is craving and the banks are worry. The current is strong, but you do not have to cross it alone.
verse.try_today: Notice the craving that rises when the mind replays the past.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)
Craving as the waves

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verse.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
verse.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.try_today: Let the replay end without trying to fix it.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet at 2am, holding a conversation from years ago, while Krishna speaks of letting go.

why: the wanting that rides on every outcome is what is set down
Peace follows at once from letting go of the fruit.

verse.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Pingala, left waiting all night by a lover who never came, finally lets go and finds peace.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
verse.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
verse.translation: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
verse.why: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
verse.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.

prasang.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
prasang.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
prasang.story_hook: Pingala sat awake listening for footsteps that never came, until she stopped listening.
prasang.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.

verse.for_you: The conversation from 2019 plays again, yet its hold on you is not fixed. You can loosen the grip of what you expected to say. Sleep is still possible for you.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you let go of an expected outcome.
verse.scene_line: Like Pingala waiting for a lover who never came, you are left alone with the night.

why: Dropping the expectation is the ease.
The waiting itself is shown as the pain, and its end as rest

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
verse.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
verse.translation: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.for_you: That conversation from 2019 has a grip on you right now. Krishna says to settle the mind little by little. Let the mind rest, and let the rest go.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet of the night, while Krishna steadies Arjuna's mind on the self.

why: the mind resting in the self
Little by little, with patience.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verse.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Bearing passing discomfort is not putting up with harm or abuse; those are not weather to wait out.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

queries.hook: I can't stop overthinking. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verse.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
verse.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: You are awake at two in the morning, replaying a conversation from years ago. The mind runs here and there, restless and to no purpose. Let the dog wander; it will tire and come back to its own door.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind runs here and there, and let it be a stray dog.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet dark, and the mind wanders far away like a stray village dog.

why: a seeker describes his own mind running everywhere for nothing
My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
verse.line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
verse.translation: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.speaker: The Ajagara sage
verse.setting: A wandering sage who lives like the python, taking what comes, explains his contentment to Prahlada.
verse.sanskrit: न सन्निपतितं धर्म्यमुपभोगं यदृच्छया / प्रत्याचक्षे न चाप्येनमनुरुध्ये सुदुर्लभम्
verse.line: I don't refuse good things that come to me, and I don't chase what's hard to get.
verse.translation: I do not refuse a rightful pleasure that comes to me on its own, nor do I go chasing after one that is hard to get.

verse.speaker: Bodhya
verse.setting: Bodhya describes another of his teachers to King Yayati: an arrow-maker lost in his work.
verse.sanskrit: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिषावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्
verse.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
verse.translation: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
verse.why: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

prasang.title: Bodhya's teachers
prasang.summary: Asked how he found peace, the sage Bodhya names his teachers: Pingala, the osprey that dropped its scrap of meat and was left alone, the snake, the deer, the arrow-maker so absorbed he did not see the king pass, and a girl's bangle.
prasang.lesson: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

verse.for_you: The king passed, and the arrow-maker saw only the arrow. Your mind has been holding that conversation since 2019, and it is still there. Let the work of this moment be your arrow. Notice its shape and nothing else.
verse.try_today: Let your hands be busy with one small task until your mind follows.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet of the night, while the arrow-maker beside you sees only his arrow.

why: Absorption as rest from distraction
Single-pointed attention to the work in hand

verse.speaker: Dattatreya
verse.setting: The wandering sage Dattatreya talks to his own restless mind.
verse.sanskrit: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥
verse.line: Friend mind, why all this chatter? It's all speculation. You are vast as the sky.
verse.translation: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
verse.why: Talk to your restless mind like a friend: why all this chatter?

prasang.title: Dattatreya's song to his own mind
prasang.summary: The wandering sage Dattatreya sings of the one Self and repeatedly turns to scold his own mind: why run around like a ghost, why all this chatter? You are vast as the sky.
prasang.lesson: Talk to your restless mind like a friend: why all this chatter?

verse.for_you: Your mind is running a conversation from 2019. That chatter is just speculation. You are the vast sky, untouched by it.
verse.try_today: Notice the mind’s chatter without feeding it. Let it pass like a cloud.
verse.scene_line: Like Dattatreya speaking to his own mind, you are vast and untouched by the old conversation.

story.title: Bhima cannot bear to wait thirteen years
story.story_hook: He found a loophole: count thirteen months as thirteen years. His brother said no.
story.summary: Bhima is sick of waiting. The years we wait, he tells Yudhishthira, are years off our lives, and death does not pause for a pledge. He even offers a scholar's loophole: the texts allow a substitute, so count the thirteen months we have already lived here as thirteen years, and let us go and fight now.
story.lesson: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
story.teaser: He found a loophole: count thirteen months as thirteen years. His brother said no.

why: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
